title: Polycrisis Resilience: Human Exposure
subtitle: Understanding and Reducing Human Exposure to Interconnected Global Risks

abstract:
Polycrisis Resilience: Human Exposure is a foundational publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).
It examines human exposure as a foundational dimension of polycrisis vulnerability, organizes exposure across six interconnected dimensions, distinguishes human exposure, human vulnerability, and Polycrisis Resilience, and establishes seven strategic development pathways to build a world in which fewer people face the conditions that generate systemic vulnerability.

keyFindings.title: Polycrisis Resilience requires transitioning from predominantly reactive crisis management toward the systematic reduction of human exposure to interconnected global risks across environmental, climatic, socioeconomic, health, infrastructural, and institutional dimensions.

Exposure reduction is not identical to vulnerability reduction: a population can remain exposed to a physical hazard while becoming substantially less vulnerable through stronger infrastructure, healthcare, institutions, and adaptive capacity.
Human exposure is highly unequal—low-income economies carry a composite exposure index of 79.0 versus 22.5 in high-income economies, driven by gaps in energy, water, housing, and governance.

Accelerating sustainable development, technological diffusion, economic convergence, environmental improvement, and institutional strengthening compresses global human exposure from 64.0 (2025) to 23.5 by 2050 and 8.5 by 2100 (-86.7%).
